zeus_t15_flip_20260822T1950Z.argument: Payoff REACHABILITY, not payoff size. (1) Fixture census: Thundergod's Wrath is learned and off cooldown on 16 frames, and on 7 of them Zeus cannot pay for it -- 4 of 12 once the four fixtures this desk cut specifically to study Zeus mana are removed. Shortfalls 26/60/98/106/123/151/239 mana, median about ONE Arc Lightning cast. (2) The taken talent cuts 20% off Arc Lightning's mana cost (85/90/95/100 -> 68/72/76/80); both of the file's builds put four points in Arc (pos_2 by level 7, pos_4/5 by level 10). (3) The rejected talent can only pay on a cast that happens, and this desk's own frame-by-frame read (GH #47, backlog 4) is 1-3 ult casts per game with 5 of 6 already killing their target.
zeus_t15_flip_20260822T1950Z.honest_bounds: The corpus is 100 frames cut for OTHER investigations: existence, not density (section Y.2). Every ult-ready frame in it is ult RANK 1, where the +75 given up is +27% of a 275-damage ult -- the larger single payout, given up on frequency grounds. Arc casts per game were NOT counted; 20% per cast repays a 106-mana shortfall only after roughly five casts between top-ups. The cooldown half of the taken talent (1.6s -> 1.28s) is near-worthless and is not part of the claim.
zeus_t15_flip_20260822T1950Z.side_findings: (a) hero_zuus.lua's ult kill-check adds talent5's 'value' to nDamage, but index 5 is special_bonus_unique_zeus_2 (+60 ARC damage, a t20 row never trained in turbo per GH #84) and its special value is named bonus_arc_damage -- the term is wrong twice and contributes nothing. Annotated, NOT repointed: whether the engine already folds talent bonuses into GetSpecialValueInt cannot be settled offline. (b) talentDamage was assigned twice and read nowhere (the shape GH #104 removed from Wraith King, GH #73 from Lion); deleted together with its only input, the talent8 handle. Behaviour-preserving.
zeus_t15_flip_20260822T1950Z.cm_t15: NO FLIP, and the reason is recorded so the next round does not re-derive it. Three code facts: (1) CONTAINMENT -- ConsiderQ's ring is GetCastRange()+aether+32 = 732 and ConsiderW's is GetCastRange()+30+aether = 630; the +100 Frostbite talent takes W's ring to 730, still inside Nova's by two units, and the aether term cancels. (2) ORDER -- SkillsComplement consults ConsiderQ before ConsiderW and returns on desire > 0, so the range talent only pays on frames Nova declined, while the rival (-4.5s Nova cooldown) pays into the consumer with first refusal. (3) BINDING CONSTRAINT -- a rank-4 Nova costs 175 with a post-talent 3.5s cooldown = 50 mana/second sustained; cooldown was never the limit, mana was. Facts 1+2 argue FOR the flip, fact 3 stops it.
zeus_t15_flip_20260822T1950Z.cm_side_findings: (a) Frostbite's cast range is 600, not the 500 the code's own attack-range floor was written against: `if #nEnemysHeroesInView <= 1 and nCastRange < bot:GetAttackRange() then nCastRange = bot:GetAttackRange() + 60 end` needs a cast range of at most 569 to fire, so it is DEAD at the shipped numbers. LEFT IN PLACE, not deleted: unreachability rests on a runtime value (GetAttackRange()), not on a zero-read local, so deleting it would be a behaviour change in any world where CM gains attack range. (b) CM has no ult mana reserve either -- the third member of the family after Zeus (GH #47/#59) and Lion (GH #73). Census: 24 ult-ready CM frames, 5 below the ult cost, one of them 399 mana against a 400 cost. The whole domain of a future reserve gate is the [ult cost, ult cost + nova cost) band = 2 frames, both at ult rank 1.

midsupyield_20260823.what: Backlog #4 'suptp x midtp 协同仲裁' (owner, state.json keep_optimize/teambrain: 'suptp needed but must COORDINATE with midtp -- response arbitration'). J.ShouldTpSupportTowerFight is shared by 'midtp' (any position) and 'suptp' (pos 4/5); the only thing separating which one answers a tower fight is J.TryTakeTpResponseSlot, a position-BLIND module-level FCFS ledger (one gated responder per 6s). So on a frame where both a core (midtp) and a support (suptp) would go, whoever asks first burns the slot -- a race. New gated soak candidate 'midsupyield': when a CORE reaches the quota take and a viable SUPPORT responder exists, the core returns nil, ceding the slot. First concrete cut of the TeamBrain phase-1 response-arbitrator ('one event -> one best responder').

midsupyield_20260823.where: bots/FunLib/jmz_func.lua: new pure predicate J.HasAvailableSupportResponder (just above J.ShouldTpSupportTowerFight) + one gated clause at the helper's quota-take call site. The soak gate lives at the CALL SITE (mirrors the [tparrive] gate on the same line); the predicate carries no gate of its own.
midsupyield_20260823.gate: turbo (inherited from the helper's first line) + J.IsSoakCandidate('midsupyield') + J.IsCore(bot). Placed BEFORE J.TryTakeTpResponseSlot so a yield never consumes the slot (Lua `and` short-circuit). Supports (pos>=4) never satisfy IsCore, so they never yield.
midsupyield_20260823.safety: SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION: the yield fires only when J.HasAvailableSupportResponder is true, i.e. a pos-4/5 teammate that is alive, level>=6, has a castable TP/BoT, and is not itself in a fight or retreating -- member-by-member the same gates the support would clear inside this helper. With no such support the core does NOT yield, so armed can only REALLOCATE a response to a support, never DROP one. Direction is also aligned with the known econ problem: it strictly REDUCES core off-farm TP participation (the residual-fingerprint defensive-gravity pull), never increases it.
midsupyield_20260823.domain: Whole-corpus census over tests/fixtures/ (966 live hero frames): the helper fires end-to-end on only 3 CORE frames; 2 of those carry a viable support responder (the yield domain), 1 does not (the negative control). campgrade_20260823.what: GH #137. The camp-tier ladder in J.Site.RefreshCamp (bots/FunLib/aba_site.lua) is dead code: four if/elseif branches that each bound botLevel from ABOVE, ending in an unconditional `else` that appends the camp anyway. A camp a low-level bot is too weak for is not stopped by its tier -- it falls THROUGH into the next, MORE permissive tier, and whatever survives is added by the else. The loop is equivalent to `allCampList = every camp on the map, at every level`. wk_bone_guard_talent_bypass_20260823T195.lever_b_verdict: The two `talent6:IsTrained()` disjuncts in X.ConsiderW are NOT a defect. sTalentList index 6 is special_bonus_unique_wraith_king_facet_3 = '+5 Bone Guard Skeletons Spawned' -- a FLAT count of skeletons per activation -- over a base min_skeleton_spawn of 0 (odota dotaconstants build/abilities.json, read 2026-08-23). wk_bone_guard_talent_bypass_20260823T195.headline_finding: X.ConsiderW is STRUCTURALLY UNVALIDATABLE ON A FIXTURE. Its first guard asks HasModifier('modifier_skeleton_king_bone_guard'); that modifier is on 0 of 34 WK frames in tests/fixtures, while 17 of those frames carry a modifier list and 17/17 carry a sibling modifier_skeleton_king_* (the denominator exists). Shipped X.ConsiderW therefore returns 0 on 34/34 real frames.
wk_bone_guard_talent_bypass_20260823T195.name_is_not_wrong: Three independent lines: (i) X.ConsiderW is the repo's only caster of the ability (grep bone_guard outside the hero file finds one weight row in FunLib/spell_list.lua, required only by hero_morphling.lua); (ii) four corpus frames catch the ability mid-cooldown against its flat 42s (cd 40.2/32.5/27.1/3.5), so the engine answered HasModifier true in those games; (iii) GH #77's l1trade ground truth records damage dealt by WK's skeletons. The gap is the pipeline: make_fixture.py rebuilds `modifiers` from PAIRED combat-log MODIFIER_ADD/REMOVE rows and there is no pair for this one.
wk_bone_guard_talent_bypass_20260823T195.one_field_counterfactual: Granting ONLY HasModifier for that name, changing nothing else, changes the outcome on 20 of 34 frames (they run past the guard into X.IsNearLaneFront and hit the loader's declared GH #61 refusal). 20 is the size of the blind spot. The other 14 stop for reasons the corpus can answer (ability unlearned / on cooldown / the level-4 floor).
wk_bone_guard_talent_bypass_20260823T195.two_further_tool_facts: (1) abilityW:GetSpecialValueInt('max_skeleton_charges') reads 0 offline (mock Get* default) => branch 1's ratio is 0/0 (NaN, false) and branch 2's equality is 0 == 0 (TRUE), i.e. the ammunition test is free. (2) The fixture loader does not implement GetModifierByName => it falls to the Get* default 0 => GetModifierStackCount(0) reads row 1 of the hero's name-sorted modifier list (measured: modifier_skeleton_king_reincarnation_scepter). -1 is the honest answer; implementing it would make X.ConsiderW's `modIdx > -1` guard start working AND would change every stack-reading branch on existing fixtures, so it is a harness-side change, not this stream's (GH #150 section 3).
wk_bone_guard_talent_bypass_20260823T195.reusable_prior: A HasModifier-shaped gate is measurable offline only if that modifier has ADD/REMOVE pairs in the combat log; with no pair the fixture world answers false forever and EVERYTHING downstream of the gate is structurally unreachable. The discriminant is desk-checkable: count how many OTHER modifiers the same hero carries in the corpus. Denominator present (here 17/17) => the 0 is a fact about that one modifier. Denominator absent => the 0 says nothing.
wk_bone_guard_talent_bypass_20260823T195.residual_registered_not_settled: If the engine only applies modifier_skeleton_king_bone_guard while charges >= 1, the guard ABOVE the disjuncts re-imposes the very ammunition requirement the bypass exists to lift, and the '+5 from an empty bank' case can never occur. Engine-internal, unanswerable from the corpus for the reasons above. Only payable at level 20 (GH #84: level >= 20 on 0 of 210 turbo hero-slots, high-water 19); GH #108 raising the game-time cap 10 -> 25 minutes is the change that would make it payable and is the trigger to re-open.

axebhpure_20260824.bug: X.ConsiderW's kill branch handed that pure claim to J.WillMagicKillTarget, which hardcodes nDamageType = DAMAGE_TYPE_MAGICAL and ends on npcTarget:GetActualIncomingDamage(EstDamage, nDamageType). Magic resistance is applied to damage the engine will not reduce => the branch under-states its own spell by at least the 25% every hero carries at base, more against any magic-resistance item (384 pure read as 288). It is NOT a house convention: X.ConsiderR in the same file declares DAMAGE_TYPE_PURE for Culling Blade and compares against RAW health with no mitigation term. axebhpure_20260824.fix: GATED 'axebhpure' (turbo-only, NOT armed). New X.WillBattleHungerKill calls the shipped J.WillMagicKillTarget FIRST and returns true on its verdict, so gate-off is byte-for-byte the shipped predicate by structure, not by measurement. Only when it has already answered false, and only when armed, does the pure arithmetic get a second opinion: nDamage * (1 + GetSpellAmp()) - GetHealthRegen() * nDelay >= GetHealth() -- i.e. J.WillMagicKillTarget with its two magical-only terms neutralised, one lever, spell amp and the 12s regeneration term both kept. The widening ABSTAINS on every target the shipped helper scales its estimate for (modifier_medusa_mana_shield, modifier_kunkka_ghost_ship_damage_delay, modifier_templar_assassin_refraction_absorb, and npc_dota_hero_bristleback by unit name), three of which cut pure damage as well, so it cannot regress any of them.

lionhexaoe_20260824.observation: aba_skill.X.GetTalentList walks bot:GetAbilityInSlot(0..25) and appends every IsTalent() ability in slot order, so sTalentList[N] means 'the Nth talent ROW entry the game ships', 1 = t10 left ... 8 = t25 right. Which talent that is, is Valve's to change, and nothing in the tree pinned it. New census tools/agent/talent_slot_census.py joins odota dotaconstants hero_abilities.json (slot order, the source GH #150 used) with the game's npc_dota_hero_<name>.txt (what each talent modifies, as an override key inside the AbilityValues block it changes).
lionhexaoe_20260824.bug: hero_lion.lua binds talent8 = sTalentList[8] and reads it FIFTEEN times to decide things about lion_voodoo (Hex): whether to pick an AoE location instead of a unit, and whether the cast-legality check may be skipped. Slot 8 today is special_bonus_unique_lion_2 = lion_impale/AbilityCastRange +600 -- it does not touch lion_voodoo. The Hex-radius talent is special_bonus_unique_lion_4 (lion_voodoo/radius +250) and it is slot 7, the OTHER half of the same t25 row. Not dormant: this file's own tTalentTreeList has ['t25'] = {10, 0}, which J.Skill.GetTalentBuild turns into index 4 = 8, so the shipped build trains exactly the half that makes those fifteen reads answer true. The file's own header prose had the row right ('t25 [7] +250 AoE Hex [8] +600 Earth Spike cast range') while the code read the other half -- prose ahead of code, the fourth time in this stream.
lionhexaoe_20260824.consequences: Two, and only the first needs the engine. (1) X.SkillsComplement swaps ActionQueue_UseAbilityOnEntity for ActionQueue_UseAbilityOnLocation while lion_voodoo's AbilityBehavior is DOTA_ABILITY_BEHAVIOR_UNIT_TARGET with no talent override anywhere in the KV -- a location order for a unit-target ability. What the engine does with that CANNOT be settled offline (no bot-side debugging), so it is registered as a RISK, never as a measured no-op. (2) `( J.CanCastOnTargetAdvanced( x ) or talent8:IsTrained() )` drops the cast-legality check on the same false premise; that half needs no engine reading to be wrong, since Hex is unit-targeted under either talent.
lionhexaoe_20260824.fix: New X.IsHexAoe in hero_lion.lua; all fifteen call sites route through it. The SHIPPED read runs FIRST and the only thing the armed path can add is `return false`, so this is a NARROWING gate whose gate-off path is the shipped path by construction -- the dual of GH #154's widening shape and the same lesson as GH #165 ('armed may only take the min'): a gate's direction is carried by the shape of the code, not by today's constants.
lionhexaoe_20260824.gate: lionhexaoe -- turbo-only, NOT armed, NOT proposed for the test set, NO queue request. Stable version undrifted.
lionhexaoe_20260824.domain: EMPTY TODAY, AND MEASURED. Every read is downstream of a level-25 talent. GH #84 read level >= 20 on 0 of 210 hero-slots (high-water 19) under SOAK_CAP_MIN=10; the test re-measures the same thing on this repo's own fixture corpus rather than citing it, and asserts max level < 25. Same disposition as alchrage: an empty domain cannot buy condition (a) however many games run. The assertion is written so it goes RED the day a level-25 hero appears (GH #108's cap 10 -> 25 is the likely cause), which is the moment this becomes proposable -- the same self-reopening shape alchrage used for SOAK_CAP_MIN.
lionhexaoe_20260824.census_limit: ONE-DIRECTIONAL, like the key census and the boots supply census: a non-empty mods list PROVES what a talent modifies; an EMPTY mods list proves nothing, because generic rows (special_bonus_hp_200) and facet rows live in npc_abilities.txt, which the census does not read. So the finding is stated through what slot 7 IS, never through what slot 8's list omits.
lionhexaoe_20260824.cross_check: The slot ordering is not taken on faith from one feed. Three claims already standing in this tree, written by earlier passes from the dota2.com datafeed, agree with the odota+KV snapshot slot for slot: hero_axe.lua:280 (7 = special_bonus_unique_axe_2, Berserker's Call radius), hero_zuus.lua's FACT block (5 = special_bonus_unique_zeus_2 on arc_lightning, 3 = the ult-damage talent special_bonus_unique_zeus_4 = zuus_thundergods_wrath/damage +75) and GH #150 (6 = special_bonus_unique_wraith_king_facet_3 on bone_guard). All six are asserted, so a feed that reshuffles turns the file red instead of silently re-anchoring it.

tbearly_20260824.defect: **Lua 没有三元运算符,`cond and x or y` 只在 `x` 永不为假时才是三元式** —— 而 `and` 比 `or` 结合更紧。`J.IsModeTurbo() and DotaTime() < 18*60 or DotaTime() < 25*60` 解析成 `(turbo and t<18*60) or (t<25*60)`,`x` 位置放的是**布尔**;又因为 18*60 < 25*60,第一个析取项**蕴含**第二个 ⇒ 整个表达式在**任何模式下**逐字等于 `DotaTime() < 25*60`。**那个 18 分钟的 turbo 常数一次都没有决定过任何事**,而且没有任何计数会报警。这是 GH #160(块 2 被块 1 支配)的**析取版孪生**:结论是两个常数之间的**算术关系**,所以用算术断言,不用帧采样 —— 帧上两条腿处处一致,看不见它。

alchrage_20260824.observation: bots/BotLib/hero_alchemist.lua and its verbatim copy bots/FunLib/rubick_hero/alchemist.lua each guarded X.ConsiderChemicalRage's Roshan and Tormentor branches with `(J.IsModeTurbo() and DotaTime() < 15*60 or DotaTime() < 30*60)` and the 16/32 twin. Lua has no ternary operator: `and` binds tighter than `or` and the `x` slot holds a COMPARISON, so it parses as `(turbo and t<15*60) or (t<30*60)`, and 15*60 < 30*60 makes the first disjunct imply the second.
alchrage_20260824.bug: Each of the four clauses was literally `DotaTime() < 30*60` (resp. 32*60) in EVERY mode. The turbo bound the author wrote decided nothing, ever, and nothing reported it -- it reads exactly like a turbo scaling somebody already did. The dead band is 15:00/16:00 to the end of a ~20-minute turbo game, i.e. a real slice of one (unlike the strategy desk's own instance in mode_farm_generic, whose 18:00-25:00 band is past the end of a turbo game). The numeric form of the same idiom, `J.IsModeTurbo() and 5*60 or 10*60` in jmz_func, is CORRECT: the discriminator is the type in the `x` slot, not the idiom.
alchrage_20260824.fix: New X.GetRageObjectiveClock(nTurboMin, nShippedMin) in both files. Gate off it returns nShippedMin*60, which is exactly what the old expression collapsed to, so gate-off equivalence is structural. The armed branch takes math.min(nClock, nTurboMin*60), so the armed predicate is a SUBSET of the shipped one whatever constants any caller passes -- a future caller handing it a turbo bound above the shipped bound still cannot widen anything. One lever.
alchrage_20260824.theory: Validation condition (c): the shipped 30:00/32:00 is a 'stop spending the ultimate on neutral objectives once fights decide the game' clock for a ~40-minute normal game. Turbo runs about half that, so the author's own 15:00/16:00 is the same rule at turbo pace. This restores intent already written down; it does not invent a bound, and it is not a claim that 15:00 is optimal (that is GH #157's clock axis, and the reason it ships gated).

The domain unblocks with GH #108 (owner's cap 10 -> 25); tests/test_alchemist_rage_objective_clock.lua asserts the cap and goes RED the day it is raised, which is the signal to propose the id.

tpdeathbuy_20260825.issue: [strategy] 本组自查(非 issue 交回)。本轮换了一根正交的轴:不是「常数对不对」(0CLK)、也不是「表达式解析出来是不是它看上去的样子」(0TERN),而是**「这个合取里的两条腿能不能同时为真」** —— 一个 SAT 层面的问题。全仓扫描 `bots/` 里所有 `if/elseif` 条件的每个析取项,把同一个左值上的多条数值比较放在一起判可满足性。**381 处时钟比较那条轴之后,这是第一条一次扫描就落到一个真缺陷上的轴。**
tpdeathbuy_20260825.defect: `bots/item_purchase_generic.lua` 的「死前如果会损失金钱则购买额外TP」块,HP 子句写的是 `botHP < 0.08 and botHP >= 1`。`botHP` 是 `J.GetHP(bot)` 的 **0..1 分数**(同文件 :653 赋值),两个界**互斥** ⇒ 整个合取**不可满足**,约 12 行是**死代码**。不是「几乎不触发」,是对**任何实数**都为假。
tpdeathbuy_20260825.provenance: **上游带来的,不是我们写坏的**:这一对逐字出现在初始 OHA 快照 `74727e4a:957-958` ⇒ 该块在本仓库历史上**一次都没有跑过**,我们任何一次测量里都不含它。
tpdeathbuy_20260825.why_stray_not_convention: 同文件往下约 35 行的**姊妹块**(辅助死前买粉)是同一个想法 —— 同样的 `botGold < (cost + botWorth/40)`、同样的 `WasRecentlyDamagedByAnyHero(3.1)`、同样的充能上限 —— 而它的 HP 腿写的是 `botHP < 0.06`,**没有配对的下界**。两个块一个有那行、一个没有,这个不对称已写成 `[reverse]` 断言:哪天有人给买粉块也补一个下界,用例红着要求重新论证。
tpdeathbuy_20260825.unit: `local bDyingWithDoomedGold = botHP < 0.08 and botHP >= 1`;armed(turbo + `tpdeathbuy`)时改成 `botHP < 0.08`。写成**选择**而不是析取(charter 0TERN 的处方)⇒ **门关着与出厂逐字相同**,而且这条同一性在这里是**算术**不是承诺:门关着的谓词仍然处处为假。
tpdeathbuy_20260825.direction_is_a_widening: ⚠ **与本组以往每一根杠杆方向相反**。以往 armed 谓词都是出厂谓词的**子集**(只可能少开火);本条 armed 是**空集的真超集** —— 它**严格增加**出厂树从不发生的采购。⇒ 波次的反向哨兵不是「TP 采购数不许塌」,而是「**TP 花费不许暴涨**」;而且**本 id 不可能被一份『无变化』读数验证**,读到无变化 = 没 armed 或域为零。
tpdeathbuy_20260825.why_worth_arming: 验证哲学条件 (c),而且是标准打法不是偏好:Dota 里英雄死亡会把身上未花的金钱按比例赔给击杀者、其余蒸发,**死前把钱花掉**是教科书习惯。块自己的金钱子句正是一条**带**而不是下限(`botGold >= tpCost` 且 `botGold < tpCost + botWorth/40` = 「我买得起,而且我手上这点钱本来就要没」)。TP 卷轴是那里最该买的东西:便宜、用掉而不是掉落、且块只在**手上 TP 不够**时开火。Turbo 里论据更强:复活快,回场的第一件事就是想 TP 回战场。
tpdeathbuy_20260825.domain: **帧域,永不与事件率相减(charter 0DOM)**。以数据方式读 104 枚 fixture 的 hp/max_hp 与 recent_damage 行(不载 jmz_func,零秒级开销):966 活英雄帧里 `botHP < 0.08` **10 帧(1.0%)**;`botHP >= 1` **347 帧**(⇒ 出厂那条上界**单独看并不空**,空的是这一对);`botHP < 0.08` **且** 3.1s 内挨过英雄伤害 = **4 帧**,四帧逐个点名钉住。其余五条腿是金钱与库存,见下。
tpdeathbuy_20260825.harness_fact_asserted: ⭐ **两条金钱腿在 fixture 上读 TRUE,而且是 0DIR 那种「带错符号的谎话」**:`GetGold()` 不在 mock 里(落 `^Get` 默认 **0**),`GetItemCost()` 答 **0**(已由 `test_fieldbuy_backpack_rescuer.lua` 钉过)⇒ `botGold >= tpCost` 是 `0 >= 0` = **TRUE**,`botGold < tpCost + botWorth/40` 是 `0 < 净值/40` = **TRUE**(净值 > 0 时)。**任何人在 fixture 上端到端驱动这个块都会得到全绿,而那份全绿对金钱带一无所证。** 两个方向都已断言:mock 哪天学会金钱,该用例红着要求重测,而不是继续看起来「已验证」。
tpdeathbuy_20260825.honest_boundary: **因此本轮不主张端到端钉帧**。可买到的本地验证是:(1) 死代码的**算术证明**(含两个常数的边界邻域点);(2) **门关着逐字同一**;(3) **方向**(armed ⊋ 出厂);(4) 语料可读的那一半域(4 帧,点名)。端到端购买动作**这份语料给不出**,没有假装给。

zusstatic_20260825.observation: zuus_static_field in this patch's KV (d2vpkr mirror, the source gen_ability_meta.py and special_value_key_census.py already read; fetched 2026-08-25) is Innate 1 / MaxLevel 1 with AbilityValues/damage_health_pct/value = 3.45 and hero_levelup = +0.05, i.e. 3.45% of the target's CURRENT health at hero level 1 rising to about 4.95% at level 31. The localisation (abilities_english.txt) says 'Zeus shocks any enemy that he attacks or is hit by his abilities, causing damage equal to a percentage of their current health' -- any enemy, creeps included, and current health, so the call sites' targets and their GetHealth() reading are both right.
zusstatic_20260825.bug: hero_zuus.lua set abilityASBonus = 0.09 whenever the passive was trained -- between 1.8x and 2.6x the KV value at every level the ability can be at. Its only two consumers are kill estimates: X.ConsiderW's ranged-creep snipe and X.ConsiderR's lowHPCount loop, the one that decides whether the ~130s map-wide execute is cashed in. The error is in the OPTIMISTIC direction, so the bot credits itself with damage it will not deal and spends the ultimate (or a 100+ mana bolt) on a target that lives. On the real frame f_230952_zuus_ult_hoard (t=567.0, level-9 Zeus, five live enemies holding 4007 HP between them) the shipped constant credits 360.6 HP of Static Field where the KV band allows 138-198: 162-222 HP invented, and every single enemy overcredited, not just the aggregate.
zusstatic_20260825.fix: New helper X.GetStaticFieldBonus( hAbility ). The shipped 0.09 is the function's LAST statement and the armed branch is the only detour, with the IsTrained() guard first, in the shipped position -- so gate-off equivalence is structural, not measured. Armed (turbo + candidate) it reads damage_health_pct and returns pct/100; a key answering <= 0 drops the term rather than restoring a fabricated default (GH #162 house rule). The handle is a PARAMETER because the file-local abilityAS is unusable offline (see limit).
zusstatic_20260825.gate: zusstatic -- turbo-only, NOT armed, NOT in the test set. Stable version undrifted.
zusstatic_20260825.limit: MEASURED, not assumed, in three places. (1) Static Field is Innate + hidden, so no .dem carries it: on the Zeus fixtures J.Skill.GetAbilityList(bot)[5] is nil and the file-local abilityAS is a handle for a nil name whose IsTrained() is false -- both legs read 0 on any untouched fixture, which is why the helper takes the handle as an argument. Same family as GH #151. (2) tests/mock/bot_api.lua answers 0 for every Get* it does not know, so GetSpecialValueFloat is 0 for every key and the armed leg offline reads 0, not 3.45 (GH #162/#133/#145). (3) GetActualIncomingDamage is 0 on every live handle (the 22nd world assertion, GH #154), so J.WillMagicKillTarget cannot be driven truthfully and 'does the ult fire on this frame' is not a fixture question. Condition (a) must be bought from the corpus: queue hero-15, criteria pre-registered there and on the issue.
zusstatic_20260825.refuted_hypothesis: 'Static Field only damages heroes, so the ConsiderW creep call site is entirely wrong' -- killed by the localisation before any code was written ('any enemy'). Only the NUMBER was wrong. Recorded because a later reader will have the same idea.
zusstatic_20260825.not_touched: Two write-only locals found in the same file and deliberately left alone (deleting them is behaviour-preserving but it is a different direction from this unit's tightening): X.ConsiderR's `local nCastRange = 1600` is referenced nowhere in that function, and X.ConsiderE's `local nJumpDistance = 450` occurs exactly once in the file. Also checked and CORRECT: X.ConsiderE's `nCastRange = 600 + nSkillLV * 100` matches KV zuus_heavenly_jump/range = 700 800 900 1000 digit for digit.
zusstatic_20260825.tests: tests/test_zuus_static_field_pct.lua -- 13 cases, 10 mutations, 9 caught + 1 honestly-recorded no-op control escaped (nPct > 0 -> >= 0, both sides return 0; reviewed and confirmed a true no-op, not a blind spot). zusboltcap_20260825.axis: 0DMG -- `ability:GetAbilityDamage()` reads that are structurally zero. New census tools/agent/ability_damage_census.py + frozen snapshot tests/mock/ability_damage.lua.
zusboltcap_20260825.observation: GetAbilityDamage() is backed by the ability's TOP-LEVEL `AbilityDamage` KV field and nothing else (docs/BOT_API_REFERENCE.md:1526). Modern Dota moved per-level damage into AbilityValues, so an ability that does not declare AbilityDamage answers 0 silently. Census over all 128 shipped heroes' KV (d2vpkr mirror, fetched 2026-08-25): 30 abilities declare AbilityDamage at all, only 16 declare a nonzero one. Against the 58 reads in bots/: 46 PROVEN-ZERO, 10 UNRESOLVED, 2 UNRESOLVED-GLOBAL. The proof needs NO handle resolution -- a read inside hero_<h>.lua can only be taken on one of <h>'s abilities, so if <h> declares no nonzero AbilityDamage the read is 0 whichever handle it was on. One-directional as always: a hero that HAS one proves nothing about a particular site. zuus_lightning_bolt's KV block has an EMPTY '// Damage.' section; its numbers live in AbilityValues/damage = 140 220 300 380.
zusboltcap_20260825.bug: hero_zuus.lua X.ConsiderW2 passed that zero as FindAoELocation's LAST argument, which is nMaxHealth. The engine rule (docs/BOT_API_REFERENCE.md:1288) is 'Pass 0 for no HP filter (target any HP)'. So the branch whose own local is named nCanKillHeroLocationAoE -- written to ask 'is there a spot where one bolt FINISHES somebody' -- has been asking 'is there an enemy hero anywhere in cast range' and answering yes at BOT_ACTION_DESIRE_HIGH, 120-135 mana a cast. That is a WIDENING. The same zero over in X.ConsiderW is fed to J.WillMagicKillTarget, where it KILLS the branch instead. One silent zero, two opposite directions, one file: which way a silent zero cuts must be read per call site -- the half GH #162's key census could not supply.
zusboltcap_20260825.fix: New helper X.GetBoltKillHealthCap( hAbility ), gated 'zusboltcap' (turbo-only). The shipped expression hAbility:GetAbilityDamage() is the function's LAST statement and the armed branch is the only detour, so gate-off equivalence is structural. Armed reads GetSpecialValueInt('damage'); a key answering <= 0 falls through to the shipped expression rather than inventing a default (the GH #162 house rule), so armed can never be WIDER than shipped. Spell amp deliberately NOT folded in -- X.ConsiderW applies it and this branch never did; adding it would be a second widening riding a tightening's gate. Direction is single (tightening only), per the GH #166 lesson.
zusboltcap_20260825.not_fixed: The other four focus-five proven-zero reads (zuus X.ConsiderW ranged-creep snipe; lion X.ConsiderQ's kill branch; lion W/E where nDamage is an unread local). Un-deadening a kill branch is a WIDENING and needs its own evidence and its own id; GH #175 section 3 files them. tests/test_zuus_bolt_kill_cap.lua ratchets their counts so a later reader cannot move them silently.
zusboltcap_20260825.validation: tests/test_zuus_bolt_kill_cap.lua -- 11 cases; mutation scan 11 mutations, 10 caught + 1 declared control escape (a pure local rename, a true no-op). cap25_boundary_20260825.what: SOAK_CAP_MIN 10 -> 25 game-minutes. Owner decision 2026-08-22 (GH #108), executed by the director 2026-08-25T09:xxZ. This entry exists so that no later reading has to guess which world a number came from.
cap25_boundary_20260825.boundary_rule: ⚠️ READINGS TAKEN ON EITHER SIDE OF THIS COMMIT ARE NOT COMPARABLE, and the reason is not only game length. Four quantities move together: (1) game length (~2.5x), (2) games per wave at fixed wall time (~/2.5), (3) the natural-end rate (near 0 -> the number GH #108 is judged by), (4) every threshold that was calibrated on an ~11-minute game. Any cross-cap comparison must state the cap of BOTH sides; a pooled reading that spans this line is void, not weak.
cap25_boundary_20260825.effective_from: the first wave launched after this commit reaches origin/main -- batch instances clone origin/main at launch, so the boundary is a REMOTE-TIP boundary, not a local one. Waves already in flight (W9, launched 06:16:33Z 2026-08-25) ran at cap=10 and are pre-boundary.
cap25_boundary_20260825.landed: soak_loop.sh (cap + a wall-clock backstop DERIVED from it, was a pinned 15 that would have killed every game ~10 game-minutes early); validate_onspot.sh (stall budget derived from the cap, was a pinned 35 min = 1.4x a single game at the new cap); analyze_log.py (natural_end field + `engine_natural`; a destroyed ancient now outranks every economic rewrite); recover_verdict.py (the gold-independent bucket is `engine_natural`, not `engine`); spot_run.sh (wave-budget guard: a watchdog that cannot outlast its own wave is refused with the --hours it needs). Pinned by tests/test_cap25_harness.py (28 checks, 5 mutations red).
cap25_boundary_20260825.winner_by_semantics: NEW: `engine_natural` = an ancient fell; the only bucket independent of gold, and its share IS the natural-end rate. `economy_25min_cap` = ran to the cap. `economy_forcewin_recovery` = sub-cap ending with NO ancient down = the referee's premature-forcewin artifact, repaired as before. The pre-boundary `engine` bucket conflated the first and third and must not be read as 'ended naturally'.
cap25_boundary_20260825.cost_rebaseline: Per-wave WALL time scales with the cap, so per-wave $ does too. The batch desk pinned $1.480/wave from the bill on 2026-08-24 (4 instances x 0.550 h x $0.673 on-demand). The same model used by the new wave-budget guard (one game ~ cap/1.8 wall-minutes; one leg = drain 1 game + ceil(12/14) games; 2 legs/seed; +12 min boot) computes 0.60 h at the OLD cap -- 9% off the measured 0.550 h, and that agreement is the only reason to extrapolate it. At cap=25 it gives 1.13 h/instance => about $3.05/wave for the SAME 12 games/leg, i.e. 2.06x, and $/effective-game rises with it. That is the price of the thing the owner bought (real wins, high-ground/buyback corpus) -- but the batch desk's $45 fence arithmetic and the efficiency ledger's $/game baseline both have to be restated at the new cap, and the pre-boundary $/game series must not be continued across this line.
cap25_boundary_20260825.domains_unblocked: Checklist item 7 (hero desk's question, GH #108 comment 2026-08-24T19:46Z): a census of gate sites carrying a time constant >= the OLD cap finds exactly two ids whose domain was constructively empty and is now reachable -- `alchrage` (armed bound 15:00/16:00, hero_alchemist + the rubick copy) and `tbearly` (band 18:00-25:00, mode_farm_generic). Both are gated, unarmed, and now proposable for the test set; neither is proposed by this entry (that is their desks' call). `lanefix`/`lf_*` also carry a 600s constant but that bundle is already rejected. Also re-opened: hero-16 (`zusboltcap`) pre-registered that its domain read of 0 must be re-measured at cap=25 and not cited from the old corpus.
cap25_boundary_20260825.open: Acceptance 1 (natural-end share / mean game length / wave cost from the first post-boundary wave) is queue director-2, batch desk. Acceptance 2 (replay desk confirms high-ground or buyback appears for the first time) rides the same wave. Threshold recalibration deferred WITH A REASON, not skipped: parse_log's 510 gpm mode line and analyze_log's 300 low_gpm line were calibrated at ~11 minutes and there is no cap=25 sample to recalibrate them ON -- guessing new constants now would be inventing them. Both are sanity flags, neither gates a verdict; director-2 asks the first wave for the avg_gpm distribution that turns the recalibration into arithmetic.

campfarm_20260825.defect: bots/mode_farm_generic.lua sweeps neutrals three times (900u x2, 1000u x1). Two of the three guard ancient camps with `bot:GetLevel() >= 10 or not nNeutrals[1]:IsAncientCreep()` -- a question about the FIRST creep of the sweep -- and the third carries no ancient clause at all. The target actually attacked comes from J.Site.FindFarmNeutralTarget(list), which reads the WHOLE list. Two camps fit inside one sweep (the bearing case has an ogre camp and an ancient camp ~590u apart), so a normal creep at [1] opens the gate while the picked target can still be ancient. For a maxHP farmer (viper/naga_siren/huskar, or any bfury/maelstrom/mjollnir/radiance holder) that is the ROUTINE outcome, not a corner case: the ancient creep has the most health on the field. The raw `Action_AttackUnit(nNeutrals[1])` fallback consults no ancient clause at any level.
campfarm_20260825.evidence: Replay desk, GH #137 comments 2026-08-24T00:59Z (200 games) and 15:57Z (all 208): on the campgrade-armed leg, 22 of 49 ancient-tier violations happened in games where NO team member ever reached the tier -- so the camp cannot have come from the camp LIST. That list-exoneration rate is 44.9% (47.9% on the 200-game read), i.e. a second path exists that the ladder does not manage. Bearing frame: spot_20260824_001230_..._2651cb/20260824_002635_slot10 spirit_breaker L8, ogre camp (-4245,357) and ancient camp (-4641,479) ~590u apart, opens on npc_dota_neutral_prowler_shaman at t=549.0.
campfarm_20260825.threshold_gap: The shipped farm family bounds ancients at 10 in THREE places -- the two mode_farm_generic clauses and utils.IsValidCreep's own `GetBot():GetLevel() > 9 or not target:IsAncientCreep()` -- while the camp ladder (campgrade) says 12. The 10..11 band is therefore the exact domain of this lever: below 10 the selectors already refuse ancients, at 12+ the ancients are legitimately allowed. This is asserted off the source, not described (world W2/W3 in the test).
campfarm_20260825.fix: New pure list filter J.Site.FilterFarmNeutrals(creepList, botLevel, bStrictAncient) in bots/FunLib/aba_site.lua (TS source in lockstep). Filter the sweep instead of re-asking about [1]: armed and below J.Site.ANCIENT_MIN_LEVEL (12, the ladder's own number, exported once so the two cannot drift), ancient creeps are not in the list at all -- so both [1] clauses, the `#nNeutrals >= 3` latch, UpdateCommonCamp, target selection and the raw fallback all agree. Gate resolved ONCE, in the file-level NeutralFarmList wrapper in bots/mode_farm_generic.lua (turbo + IsSoakCandidate('campfarm')); all three sweeps go through it and the test asserts that CALL-SITE COUNT rather than trusting the edit.

The shipped `>= 10` clauses are left exactly where they are -- nothing was tidied up.
campfarm_20260825.declared_consequence: When the only creeps in the sweep are ancient ones, the armed list is EMPTY, and the farm block then takes its OWN existing empty-sweep path (re-pick a camp / walk to the camp location) -- an existing branch, not a new one this fix invents. Armed together with campgrade the two overlap only in outcome, never in mechanism; campfarm is the only one of the three that touches the raw Action_AttackUnit fallback.

cmboots_RESOLVE_20260825T2130Z.condition_c: NOT SATISFIED AS FILED, on four legs. (1) THE RULE'S OWN TEST RETURNS THE OPPOSITE FOR THIS HERO. Iron rule 2(c) names web-retrievable standard strategy as the corroboration method. Retrieved 2026-08-25: the standard boot for Crystal Maiden is Tranquil Boots, and the reason given is Arcane Aura plus Tranquil's own regen, i.e. exactly the claim the request needs to establish ('CM has no mana item, therefore she should buy one') has already been considered and rejected in standard play FOR THIS HERO SPECIFICALLY. (2) THE OBVIOUS REBUTTAL WAS CHECKED BY THE DIRECTOR AND DOES NOT HOLD. The rebuttal available to the hero desk is that the aura is weak across the scored window: tests/mock/special_value_shapes.lua:293 gives base_mana_regen 0.4/0.6/0.8/1 and proximity_bonus_factor 3 => 1.2 mana/s in-radius at rank 1, and hero_crystal_maiden.lua:19's level-up queue {1,2,3,2,2,6,2,1,1,1,6,3,3,3,6} puts the aura's second point at hero level 12, so the batch's 10-min-capped window is scored at 40% aura. TRUE BUT NON-DISTINGUISHING: the human standard build also holds Arcane Aura at one point until late and still chooses Tranquil, so this fact is already priced into the advice in (1). It does not separate bot from human and therefore cannot rescue (c). (3) THE ONE GENUINELY BOT-SPECIFIC MEASUREMENT POINTS UPSTREAM, NOT AT THE BOOTS. The request measured, but did not draw the conclusion from, this: teammates cast Replenish 2.8-4.4 times per game while CM RECEIVES 0.00-1.07 (1200 radius); frame example 1d9ae5/033503_slot9 has lina and zuus casting 11 times and CM receiving 0. The same 1200 is Arcane Aura's proximity_bonus_radius. So one positioning pathology is simultaneously eating her own aura's 3x proximity bonus AND the team's Replenish. 'CM has no mana item' is the symptom; 'CM stands outside the team's mana radius' is the cause, and the cause is free to move while the boots cost 375g. (4) THE LEDGER IS NOT NEUTRAL, IT IS NEUTRAL-WITH-A-COST. Bought: +2.04 casts/game, mp<100 -3.5pp (read as a floor -- offline there is no per-ability mana table and 100 is below every CM ability). Deaths two layers opposite sign => not read (iron rule 4(i)). And on the win side, +7.03 gpm sits INSIDE this same wave's own structural null leg (|-5.41| gpm, seed 888) => (b) bought 'no clear negative', it did not buy 'this helps'. The purpose of the owner's three-condition rule is to spare well-grounded harmless changes from significance testing; it is not a route by which a change whose stated grounding retrieves backwards, and whose ledger carries a two-layer same-sign cost, ships on 'it did not get worse'.

campdanger_20260826.issue: GH #193 (hero group hand-off 2026-08-25T22:55Z, out of the call-form census in GH #192)
campdanger_20260826.defect: bots/mode_farm_generic.lua Think() negated a call to a J.Site field named IsCampDangerous. The name is declared in no file under bots/ under any of the six declaration forms, and J.Site is require(FunLib/aba_site), a transpiled module of plain `____exports.name = function` assignments with no setmetatable and no __index -- so no dynamic fall-back exists and the field is nil. The line raised `attempt to call a nil value` INSIDE Think(). The engine's error handler is broken and print() never reaches the console, so it never read as a crash: it read as a SILENT Think abort, UNGATED, in every game, on every frame where a farming bot's nearest available camp was >200u closer than its current pick. Everything below that point in Think() -- the entire preferedCamp block that walks to the camp and attacks the neutrals -- was eaten on those frames.
campdanger_20260826.why_it_was_never_caught: tests/test_no_undefined_jmz_refs.lua (GH #48) asserts exactly this class and runs every round, but its pattern stops at the first dot: `J%.([%w_]+)` reads `J.Site.IsCampDangerous` as a reference to `J.Site`, which IS defined (jmz_func.lua:29, `J.Site = require(...)`), so the second component was never asked about. The blind spot covers every name under J.Site / J.Skill / J.Item / J.Role / J.Utils / J.Chat -- 78 distinct sub-table calls, of which this was the only unresolvable one, but the other 77 had nothing guarding them either. luacheck cannot see it (.luacheckrc is only={'1'}, i.e. 1xx global access, and this is a field access on a legitimate local). The arity census cannot see it (census() skips names with no declaration before stats). Runtime cannot see it (broken error handler).

(ii) The interpreter is BOUGHT before it is declared missing: bounded (timeout 120), guarded (apt-get present; root or passwordless sudo), silent on failure -> falls through to (i), i.e. today's behaviour plus a banner. That refusal is about mutating the WORKING TREE -- a selfcheck dying between stash and pop strands a session's uncommitted work. Installing a package touches no repo state and can strand nothing. The suite output was redirected to a file while I tailed the task wrapper's own 22-byte '[exited with code 0]'; the redirect target was block-buffered and looked empty for tens of minutes. Same family as GH #200 (zero test bodies, exit 0) and GH #171 (SKIP that does not lift the exit code): a reading with no content and a reading of 'none' are the same shape, and telling them apart means looking at a DIFFERENT field (exit code / file size / is the process still alive) -- I looked at none of them before writing a negative claim. Second lesson: the tree was rebased mid-run, so I re-ran to disambiguate -- but `git diff --stat ba11ce59 9d16d600` is TWO markdown files, neither in the Lua runner's read set, so the first reading was never tainted. talentvalue_20260826.observation: Third axis of the talent-binding family, after BY INDEX (GH #166/#214) and BY LITERAL NAME (GH #223). Not which talent the handle names -- whether that handle can answer `value` at all. Talents come in two families and only one owns a `value`: GENERIC talents (special_bonus_hp_200, special_bonus_strength_15) are real ability blocks in npc_abilities.txt, each carrying exactly one AbilityValues entry named `value`; HERO-UNIQUE talents (special_bonus_unique_axe_2) have NO KV block anywhere -- not in npc_abilities.txt, not in the hero's own npc_dota_hero_<h>.txt. Their payload lives inside the MODIFIED ABILITY's entry as a sub-key named after the talent. So a unique talent handle answers no key at all and talent:GetSpecialValueInt('value') is a silent 0 (BOT_API_REFERENCE: 'a typo will silently return 0').

talentvalue_20260826.the_load_bearing_reading: The dead term is dead in the SAFE direction, and the obvious repair is the regression. The KV shape (`"radius" { "value" "315"  "special_bonus_unique_axe_2" "+85" }`) exists so the engine can fold +85 into `radius` for a caster who trained the talent; there is nowhere else the bonus could live, so if the engine did not fold it the talent would do nothing in the game at all. Hence abilityQ:GetSpecialValueInt('radius') ALREADY carries the bonus and repointing the term at a handle that answered would DOUBLE-COUNT. abilvalue_20260826.observation: GH #228 measured `'value'` reads on TALENT handles. This is the same key read on ORDINARY ABILITY handles. An ability's special values are keyed by the ENTRY NAME inside its AbilityValues block; in the modern long form (`"avalanche_damage" { "value" "90 180 270 360"  "special_bonus_unique_tiny" "+90" }`) `value` is an INNER key of the entry, not an entry of the ability. So GetSpecialValueInt('value') on an ability asks for an entry that does not exist and gets the documented silent 0, unless that ability literally owns an entry NAMED `value` -- which is exactly how a GENERIC talent block is written, and is why the same string answers on one family of handles and not the other.
abilvalue_20260826.measurement: 8 live sites, 7 distinct abilities, 6 HTTPS GETs (npc_heroes.txt for ability->hero ownership, then the 5 hero KVs that actually have a site), zero AWS. NOT ONE of the 7 abilities owns an entry named `value` -- 8 of 8 READS-ZERO. Sites: hero_tiny.lua Avalanche, hero_enigma.lua Malefice x2 / MidnightPulse / BlackHole, hero_gyrocopter.lua RocketBarrage, hero_enchantress.lua Impetus, hero_terrorblade.lua DemonZeal. Focus five: ZERO sites on this axis -- GH #228's probe (2) had already bought that negative, and it holds.
abilvalue_20260826.the_load_bearing_reading: THE SIGN IS THE OPPOSITE OF GH #228'S, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF COUNTING IT SEPARATELY. #228's 21 sites all reduced to harmless: a hero-unique talent's bonus has no second home, so the engine must fold it into the base number the site already read, and repairing the term would DOUBLE-COUNT. All 21 of 21 dead on the safe side. Nothing folds here -- these sites are not adding a bonus to a number they already have, the read IS the number and the number is 0. Split: 5 UNDER (a damage or multiplier of 0 handed straight to J.CanKillTarget, so the finisher branch can never fire -- tiny Avalanche, enigma Malefice base and BlackHole, gyrocopter RocketBarrage, enchantress Impetus), 1 OVER (terrorblade DemonZeal reads its health cost as free, so the post-cast HP guard binds on nothing), 2 FOLD (the only two of #228's harmless kind). Two of eight on the safe side, not eight of eight.
abilvalue_20260826.the_obvious_repair_is_wrong_at_the_over_: The key hero_terrorblade.lua wants is `health_cost_pct`, whose KV value is 20 -- twenty PERCENT, not a fraction -- while the line multiplies by CURRENT HEALTH directly (bot:GetHealth() * <read>). Swapping the key alone turns a cost of 0 into 20x the hero's health, and the guard it feeds ((hp - cost)/maxhp > 0.5) flips from always-true to never-true: the ability would go from always permitted to never cast. The repair is two edits (`health_cost_pct` AND `/ 100`), never one. Same family as #228's lesson in the other direction: on that axis the obvious repair double-counted, on this one it inverts a guard. A claimant reading only the intended-key column would ship exactly the wrong half, so the source annotation says so and tests/test_ability_value_read_anchor.lua section 4 pins that it keeps saying so.
abilvalue_20260826.two_axes_land_on_one_branch: hero_enigma.lua's MidnightPulse radius branch is wrong twice over, independently. (1) `'value'` is not a key of enigma_midnight_pulse -- this axis. (2) The talent it is gated on is misnamed: MidnightPulseRadiusTalent binds special_bonus_unique_enigma_6, which the KV says modifies enigma_black_hole/damage (+50); the talent that widens this radius is special_bonus_unique_enigma_9 (+200). That second half was already registered by GH #223 section 6.3 as a lead nobody had priced. Both are now cross-referenced in the source, and its repair is DELETION either way -- `radius` already folds the trained talent.
abilvalue_20260826.the_ordinal_is_load_bearing: A site's identity is (file, variable, nth-read-of-that-variable) -- never the line number (GH #221; this change's own annotations moved all eight lines). The ordinal is NOT decoration, and hero_enigma.lua is why: it reads `Malefice` twice and the two reads want OPPOSITE repairs -- the first a key (`stun_instances`, 3/3/3/3), the second DELETION, because stun_instances already folds special_bonus_unique_enigma_2 (+4) and a key there double-counts. A census keyed on (file, var) alone would have to hand both rows one instruction, and either choice is wrong for one of them. Driven as a mutation (M3, ordinal pinned to 1) and caught.

Each names the ability's real entry list, the intended key (or that the repair is deletion), and that repairing it is a gated + real-frame job on a non-focus hero rather than annotation work. abilvalue_20260826.deliberately_not_repaired: All five heroes are non-focus, and every repair here is a genuine behaviour change (0 -> a real number in a kill predicate, or a cost guard that starts binding), not a nil-guard of the #192/#223 kind that lands ungated. Charter discipline says a behaviour change ships gated behind a soak candidate AND pinned by a real frame; there is no corpus for these five heroes and buying one is a batch-desk cost for heroes the project is not polishing. So the axis is COUNTED and REGISTERED with the repair spelled out per site, and the repairs are handed off. abilvalue_20260826.the_expensive_line: The anchor's terrorblade marker went red on its first run -- against the very annotation it exists to protect -- because the phrase 'twenty PERCENT, not a fraction' WRAPPED across two comment lines in the source. Third time this family has been paid for: GH #223's M8 marker and GH #228's retraction marker both escaped a first draft the same way. An assertion aimed at prose has to be aimed at prose that does not wrap, and the cheap fix is to put the load-bearing phrase on its own line in the SOURCE rather than to loosen the assertion.
abilvalue_20260826.honest_bounds: (1) `sign` is this desk's reading of the arithmetic downstream of each read, recorded by hand in the census and NOT derived -- the tool proves the read is 0, not that the branch matters. NOBODY HAS COUNTED how often these branches are reached in play; that needs a corpus and none of these five heroes is focus-five. (2) The anchor is a CONSISTENCY ratchet, not a correctness one: snapshot and tree can be wrong together and stay green. (3) Nothing here evaluates the engine -- the mock answers 0 for every key on every handle (GH #100/#133/#145/#154 family), so no fixture run can tell a right key from a wrong one, which is exactly why this axis is settled from the KV. (4) Full `lua5.1 tests/run_tests.lua` did not produce a reading this round (GH #124, ~100min); recorded as DID NOT RUN, not as passed. trunk already carries 2 reds (GH #216, not this desk's).

salveyield_20260827.shape: **本轮没有常数可推导,于是干脆不引入常数。** 比例与绝对血量对「谁更惨」给出不同答案,而大药是**定量**治疗(400),两种读法都说得通:比例挑「按分数最接近死」的,绝对挑「最小一发爆发就死」的,而 400 血对辅助是大半个池子、对核心是一条缝。与其挑一根轴(再挑一个边际常数)让语料读数好看,不如**只在支配关系成立时让位**:队友必须**在两种读法上同时更惨**。那是两条候选规则的**交集**,因此按构造就是其中**最保守**的一条,而且**没有任何阈值可拟合**。`[source]` 断言 helper 函数体里**除了 0 不许出现任何数字**(0 是保持交叉相乘方向有效的正性守卫,不是可调参数),并断言两个 getter **每个英雄各读一次**(比较不可能读到同一个英雄的两个数)。比例比较写成**交叉相乘**而非两次除法 ⇒ 不需要 epsilon、不可能除零。
salveyield_20260827.direction: **永不丢弃施法,只改变目标。** 调用点把贴队友那半**自己的开火条件**(选出了队友 ∧ consider 的敌人表为空)命名为 `bAllyBranchOpen` 并**同帧传给** helper;helper 在它为假时**短路返回 false**。于是让位只可能把控制权交给一条**已知会对同一个队友返回 HIGH** 的分支 ⇒ armed 帧的效果严格是**换目标**,绝不会出现「药这一帧没人喝」。`[nodrop]` 四条断言把这条性质**从源码文本里读出来**(不是从模型里)。依据 (c):一次性消耗品应当落在更惨的那个人身上,是标准打法;注意这一处**姊妹 lotus 并不站在我们这边**(它自用也是直接 return),所以本条的依据**不是「树上已经这么说了」**,这一点写在 helper 注释里没有含糊。

lvlpremise_20260827.observation: GH #84's turbo level census read `level >= 20` on 0 of 210 hero-slots, high-water 19. That reading was correct about the corpus and wrong about turbo: every batch game self-terminated at a 10-minute economy cap, so no hero-slot COULD reach 20. It was then written into the shipped Lua of four focus heroes as the reason the t20/t25 rows of tTalentTreeList were never examined, and into tests/test_focus_talent_anchor.lua as the reason they were never pinned.
lvlpremise_20260827.what_falsified_it: Owner priority P3 (GH #108) raised the batch cap to 25 minutes. The first frame taken past it -- iterations/pending/tpgap_159_fixture/f_260826_155416_slardar_tpgap.lua, t=1382.2 (23:02) of a 24.9-minute naturally-ended game, GH #235 -- reads ten heroes at level 22-27, high-water 27. lvlpremise_20260827.the_load_bearing_reading: t20 and t25 are LIVE rows, and the ten picks they resolve to across the focus five have never been argued in this project -- they are the OpenHyperAI snapshot's defaults, inherited and never read. First pricing table recorded in tests/test_focus_talent_anchor.lua, one comment block per hero: axe [5]/[7], zuus [5]/[7], skeleton_king [6]/[7], lion [6]/[8], crystal_maiden [6]/[7].
lvlpremise_20260827.the_sharpest_consequence: Lion. His t25 row is {10,0} = index [8] = special_bonus_unique_lion_2 (+600 Earth Spike cast range) -- exactly the half that makes every `talent8` read in hero_lion.lua answer TRUE while the code believes it means 'Hex is an area spell now' (GH #166; the Hex-radius talent is [7], the other half of the same row). From level 25 a shipped turbo Lion trains [8], X.IsHexAoe answers true, and the W dispatch swaps ActionQueue_UseAbilityOnEntity for ActionQueue_UseAbilityOnLocation on a UNIT_TARGET ability. GH #166 landed the narrowing as soak candidate 'lionhexaoe' and ruled its domain EMPTY -- on the corpus that could not reach 25. THAT RULING RESTS ON THE RETIRED PREMISE. Re-open #166; do not read the empty domain forward.
lvlpremise_20260827.the_second_consequence_points_the_other_: Axe reads BOTH talent7 and talent8. A hero takes ONE talent per tier, and his t25 row is {0,10} = [7]. So talent7 is live from level 25 -- the `nRadius + talent7:GetSpecialValueInt('value')` line really runs now, adds 0, and GH #228 says that is CORRECT because the engine folded the +85 into the base radius already; what changed is that the ruling used to ALSO be protected by unreachability and the fold argument is now the only thing holding it. And talent8 is STRUCTURALLY UNTRAINED: its nKillDamage term is dead code, not merely a zero read. Whoever takes the registered `hero-2` lever inherits both halves.
lvlpremise_20260827.the_worry_that_turned_out_unfounded_and_: ability_item_usage_generic.lua consumes sSkillList strictly from the head and does NOT skip an entry it cannot level -- the only escape is guarded by `botLevel > 25`. So a talent queued before its tier would stall everything behind it. Driven out of the real J.Skill.GetSkillList: talents land at list positions 10, 15, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23. That reads wrong and is right, because a list position is the Nth ability point SPENT (which is how the consumer itself reads it: nPointsSpent = botLevel - bot:GetAbilityPoints()). 15 ability points plus one at each of 10/15/20/25 puts position 18 at level 20 and position 19 at level 25 exactly. Positions 20-23 are the other half of each already-taken tier, permanently unlevelable -- and never dequeued, because there is no 20th point. 'The tail is dead weight' is true; 'the tail jams the queue' is not, and they are different claims.
lvlpremise_20260827.world_assertion_registered_not_asserted: That a hero receives an ability point at levels 1-15 and at 10/15/20/25 and at no other level. Nothing offline evaluates it (the mock answers a constant for GetAbilityPoints()), and it is the only thing that makes queue positions 18/19 MEAN levels 20/25. If it is wrong, the pinned positions are still right and their interpretation is wrong -- which is the failure worth being able to find later.
lvlpremise_20260827.the_blast_radius_and_why_it_is_split: The premise is quoted at 9 sites in 4 shipped hero files and at 20 sites across 9 test files. Behind several of the test-side ones it is not prose but the ARGUMENT of a verdict. Re-reading a verdict is work; rewriting a sentence is not, and mixing them would let cheap edits stand in for expensive re-reads. So: bots/ corrected in full and held at ZERO uncorrected sites as an equality (it is the Workshop deliverable and the one place a reader meets the claim with no test beside it); tests/ registered as a CEILING of 9 files over a closed list, which may fall as each verdict is genuinely re-read and may not rise.
lvlpremise_20260827.what_corrected_means_here: NOT deleting the quote. The premise should stay quoted -- the verdicts written on top of it are unreadable without it (same shape as section 4 of test_focus_talent_anchor.lua: the stale ladder may be quoted, never used). A site counts as corrected when its own comment block names GH #235 or the 2026-08-27 correction within 14 lines. So the ratchet cannot be satisfied by censorship, only by writing down what replaced the claim; an anti-vacuum assertion (>= 9 quoted sites must survive in bots/) enforces that directly.

lvlpremise_20260827.the_expensive_line: A mutation harness that reverts with `git checkout --` destroys UNCOMMITTED work in the same file. The bots/ mutation round reverted four hero files and silently wiped that round's corrections to them; only crystal_maiden survived because it was not in the checkout list. Cost: one redo of seven edits. The cheap rule is to save a copy first and restore from the copy -- never from git -- or to commit before mutating. Same family as the charter's rule-10 warning about the selfcheck dying between stash and pop.
lvlpremise_20260827.honest_bounds: The registry is a PROSE ratchet: it proves a premise-bearing comment acknowledges the correction, and proves nothing about whether the verdict built on that premise was re-read. A file can pass it and still hold a stale INERT. The fingerprints are the literal forms the claim took in this repo as of 2026-08-27; a tenth phrasing would not be caught, which is why bots/ is an equality and not merely a ceiling. The counter-example frame is NOT LANDED -- it sits in iterations/pending/ because GH #236 gives the ordering decision to the director -- so nothing here depends on it being in tests/fixtures/; it is cited as evidence, read directly from that file. Nothing in this round prices any of the ten t20/t25 picks; recording what a row takes is not arguing that it should.
lvlpremise_20260827.deliberately_not_done: Not one talent row was changed. Ten unexamined picks is not a reason to change ten picks in the round that discovered they were live -- a talent pick ships UNGATED by charter rule, so it is a live behaviour change in every turbo game, and the standing lesson is that locally-correct is not emergently-good. Pricing them is the next baton, one hero at a time, each with condition (c) written into its own hero file.

liont25_20260827.why_1_standard: +250 Hex radius is Lion's marquee t25: it converts a single-target 4s disable into a team-wide one centred on the target. +600 Earth Spike cast range adds no disable and no damage, only delivery distance. Deliberately listed FIRST and called the WEAKEST of the three grounds, because it is the one anyone can look up and therefore the one that carries no local evidence.
liont25_20260827.why_2_bot_specific: The half that is ours. lion_voodoo is DOTA_ABILITY_BEHAVIOR_UNIT_TARGET, so the engine applies the +250 radius on cast: a bot collects the ENTIRE talent with zero aiming, zero prediction and zero new code. lion_impale is a LINE skillshot with travel time -- the one ability on this hero that must be led -- and [8] would raise its cast range 500 -> 1100, more than doubling the lead distance on the ability the bot is worst at. So the two talents are not merely unequal, they are unequal in the direction that MATTERS FOR A BOT: [7] is worth more to a bot than to a human and [8] is worth less.
liont25_20260827.why_3_structural_repair: It removes GH #166's defect BY CONSTRUCTION rather than gating around it. Fifteen reads in hero_lion.lua ask `talent8` whether Hex is an area spell, while slot 8 is the Earth-Spike-range half and does not touch lion_voodoo at all. A hero trains ONE talent per tier, so with the row on [7] `talent8` is structurally untrained, X.IsHexAoe answers false everywhere, and FALSE IS THE CORRECT ANSWER for a unit-target ability under either talent: the entity dispatch is kept and the cast-legality check is no longer skipped. Nothing is lost, because the engine applies the radius whether or not this file knows about it.
liont25_20260827.what_is_given_up: Stated up front so it is not discovered later as a surprise: the J.GetAoeEnemyHeroLocation branch in X.ConsiderW (the 'W-团控' one) is skipped when IsHexAoe is false, so the bot no longer PREFERS a clustered target once it really does have AoE Hex. That is a missed optimisation, not a defect -- the most-dangerous-enemy branch directly below it serves the same fight and was verified by reading -- and it is a WIDENING, which GH #166 section 9 deliberately left to a later hand. Filed forward, not silently absorbed.
liont25_20260827.t20: PRICED AND NOT CHANGED. The row already takes [6] (special_bonus_unique_lion_10, Earth Spike 30-degree cone), which is the side this desk argues for anyway: unconditional, and it buys the same aiming forgiveness as ground 2 -- a cone forgives the lateral error a bot's lead makes on a line skillshot. [5] (special_bonus_unique_lion_8, +20 Finger damage per kill) banks stacks only after Finger KILLS and arrives at level 20, late in a ~20-minute turbo game. Recorded so [6] stops reading as an unexamined default and does not get re-priced from zero.
liont25_20260827.gate_disposition: 'lionhexaoe' STAYS, unarmed and unproposed, and the reason CHANGED. GH #166 ruled its domain empty because no hero in the fixture corpus reached level 25 -- a ruling that inherited GH #84's zero, which belonged to the 10-minute economy cap and not to turbo. That premise was retired at 02:15Z. The domain is still empty, now for a STRUCTURAL reason that depends on no corpus: the row takes [7], so talent8 is never trained and X.IsHexAoe returns false at its first statement, before the gate is consulted. The gate is kept because neither the t25 row nor Valve's slot order is hero_lion.lua's to guarantee -- if either moves, the guard is the only thing between that change and fifteen location orders on a unit-target ability.

REACHABILITY, and it is the strongest keep-case in the focus five: [6] is the ONLY talent in this hero's tree the shipped decision layer reads. talent6:IsTrained() is the OR-bypass on BOTH branches of X.ConsiderW, and what it bypasses is the bank threshold this file's own GH #17 block argues is near-unreachable (cap 8 by hero level 7, on the hero the batch reads at 15 last hits / 0.6 kills a game). talentblind_20260827.verdict: THE CORPUS IS BLIND TO HERO-UNIQUE TALENTS. 960 hero-frames across 105 fixtures carry 67 talent sightings; every one is a GENERIC row (special_bonus_hp_200 / _attack_damage_25 / _movement_speed_20 / ...). Hero-unique (special_bonus_unique_*) rows appear ZERO times -- on any hero, at any level. No frame ever carries more than ONE talent, and the 9 frames at level >= 15 (where the game guarantees at least two trained talents) carry none. So a corpus read of 'was this unique talent trained' can only ever come back zero, and that zero is not evidence -- same shape as GH #238, where the zero was a property of the 10-minute cap rather than of turbo.
talentblind_20260827.why_not_vacuous: The focus five have SINGLE-ROW talent tables, so their shipped t10 pick is decidable offline via aba_skill.X.GetTalentBuild ({0,10} -> slot 1, {10,0} -> slot 2). Generic picks are seen by name on the hero that picks them; unique picks never are.
talentblind_20260827.undecided: Two accounts survive and are observationally identical from a dump. H1 INSTRUMENT: the dumper drops unique talents -- isRealAbility() in tools/batch_test/behavioral/dumper/main.go discards Special_Bonus_Base / Special_Bonus_Attributes BEFORE the branch that keeps leveled talents, and that first line only does work on an entity that IS leveled (an untrained talent is already dropped by level > 0 on the next line); the surviving names are CLASS names, not KV names (special_bonus_h_p200, never the KV's special_bonus_hp_200). H2 WORLD: the bots never train a unique talent and the point is banked. Consequences differ enormously (H1 = every corpus talent read is blind; H2 = five rounds priced rows nobody takes).
talentblind_20260827.tiebreak_evidence: 27 fixtures both SHOW one hero's talent and HIDE another's inside the same frozen instant -- an instrument cannot be blind and not-blind in one frame. campvoid_20260828.domain_ruling: GH #265 §4 asked BUGGY or SILENT and said the two are inseparable offline. Read off the source, a THIRD reading fits every frame and needs no mode read: campfarm's own path was working exactly as designed (armed, under-tier, the attack list IS empty, so no Action_AttackUnit is issued -- which is precisely why ES logged ZERO damage events of its own over 19 seconds while dying). The waste is not that the bot attacked an ancient; it is that emptying the attack list did not also release the bot from the camp. That reading is consistent with §1 in full. It does NOT explain §2's bristleback first blows at L11 (a DAMAGE event against black_dragon exists there), so §2 remains BUGGY-or-SILENT and is NOT claimed closed by this lever.
